title: Control Room 1986
tagline: Type the orders that bring every flight home.
teaser: Clock in at a green phosphor radar and talk planes through your sector one typed order at a time: climb, turn, circle, land. Jets and props arrive from the edges and the airports, the radio reads back every call, and the shift runs until a plane is lost. How many can you bring home?

manPage.synopsis: atc — type a plane’s letter and an order; land it or send it out, and keep every pair apart.
manPage.description: The owner’s earlier typed-radar port of Ed James’s atc, kept as it was built: a phosphor console, the original’s command letters and a radio that reads back every order. A second interpretation beside the collection’s own atc.

howToPlay: Type a plane’s letter, then an order: Aa9 climbs plane A to 9,000 feet, Atd turns it east.
Land at altitude 0 along the runway arrow; leave by the right exit at 9,000 feet.
Keep planes apart and fuelled: the shift ends when one is lost.
